indication: Indolent Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (follicular lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma)
investor_note: This multi-arm Phase 1/2 study aims to establish the RP2D/safety profile of EO2463 (a novel vaccine) as monotherapy and in combination with lenalidomide and/or rituximab in indolent NHL, with Phase 2 ORR and complete response rate as co-primary endpoints. Key caveats are the non-randomized, open-label, single-arm design with no comparator arm, limiting causal efficacy conclusions — results would be hypothesis-generating for a potential registrational combination strategy.

This single-arm Phase 2 study evaluates rulonilimab (a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) combined with platinum-based chemotherapy in first-line advanced/metastatic NSCLC, with ORR as the key signal-generating endpoint across non-squamous and squamous cohorts. A meaningful ORR signal in either cohort would support the hypothesis that bispecific immune-priming enhances chemotherapy response in NSCLC, though the single-arm, open-label design limits causal inference without a comparator arm.

This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 trial tests whether hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBO) can reduce CIPN symptoms and improve patient-reported QoL (EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 subscales) in breast cancer patients on nab-paclitaxel — a supportive-care question, not a drug approval catalyst. The key watch item is whether the patient-reported outcome scale demonstrates clinically meaningful improvement that could support broader adoption of HBO as a supportive therapy; the open-label design and surrogate endpoint limit direct regulatory translation.

This single-arm Phase 2 study tests whether combining the small molecule utidelone (an HDAC inhibitor) with bevacizumab (anti-VEGF mAb) can generate meaningful PFS signal in heavily pre-treated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer — a population typically unresponsive to targeted agents. The absence of a comparator arm and use of PFS (rather than OS) limit the ability to draw definitive efficacy conclusions; results would be hypothesis-generating for a potential registrational combination strategy. Key caveats are the single-arm design, open-label conduct, surrogate PFS endpoint, and the already challenging nature of targeting this residual/relapsed indication.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates the cisplatin + 5-FU + nimotuzumab regimen in treatment-naïve metastatic NPC, with ORR and PFS as co-primary endpoints; a meaningful response rate would support further development of nimotuzumab (a EGFR monoclonal antibody) in this niche. The absence of a comparator arm, open-label design, and surrogate endpoints limit direct registrational utility without further controlled study.

indication: Solid tumors with metastases to soft tissue
investor_note: This investigator-sponsored trial tests whether adding autologous CD1c+ myeloid dendritic cells (myDCs) to a standard ipilimumab + AS01B intratumoral regimen and concurrent IV nivolumab improves efficacy and tolerability in solid tumors with soft tissue metastases. With only 18 estimated patients and a safety/feasibility primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating signal-finding study — not a registrational catalyst.

This Phase 1 dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD and tolerability of bortezomib (a proteasome inhibitor) combined with cisplatin in recurrent/metastatic breast cancer — a historically chemo-resistant indication. With only 20 estimated enrollees and a DLT/MTD primary endpoint, this is a safety de-risking step; any efficacy signal would be purely exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the intraperitoneal platinum-based regimen PIPAC to standard cisplatin/pemetrexed chemotherapy improves OS in 1L abdominal mesothelioma — a historically poor-prognosis indication. The trial is currently suspended, which is the dominant risk flag and materially clouds any near-term catalyst thesis until the hold is lifted and data is reviewed.

indication: Hematologic malignancies (ALL, AML, CML, MDS, MPN, DLBCL), allogeneic HCT setting
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether adding 300,000 IU of vitamin A and 100,000 IU of vitamin D to the conditioning regimen reduces cumulative incidence of GI acute GVHD in allogeneic HCT for multiple hematologic malignancies — a supportive-care question with no direct drug or device investment angle. Investor relevance is limited to potential sponsor or partner interest in nutraceutical conditioning strategies, though the open-label design, academic sponsorship, and GI-GVHD surrogate endpoint keep this on the fringe of meaningful commercial catalyst.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated high-dose cytarabine followed by clofarabine in relapsed/refractory AML and ALL, with patient response at 5 weeks as the key signal. Without a comparator arm, any efficacy readout is hypothesis-generating only and cannot establish incremental benefit of clofarabine over standard high-dose cytarabine alone.

This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation study sought to establish the MTD and safety profile of ombrabulin (a microtubule-targeting agent) combined with bevacizumab (anti-VEGF mAb) in advanced solid tumors, with PK and RP2D as co-primary endpoints. With only 39 patients enrolled and a DLT-based design, this is strictly a safety/dose-finding exercise — any anti-tumor signal would be purely exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

This first-in-human dose-escalation and expansion study aims to establish the MTD, safety profile, and early efficacy signal for DB-1305/BNT325 (a novel combination of a PD-1 inhibitor and a B7-H3-targeting antibody) across advanced solid tumors, with pembrolizumab added to the regimen in Phase 2. The key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any RP2D or response signal that could support a registrational combination; however, the Phase 1/2a design, open-label structure, and a 2027 primary completion date represent meaningful execution and timeline risk.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated BKM120, a PI3K inhibitor, in TNBC — a subtype with limited targeted options and poor prognosis — with clinical benefit rate as the key signal. The absence of a comparator arm and surrogate endpoint limit direct efficacy conclusions; results are hypothesis-generating for PI3K pathway inhibition in TNBC.

This randomized Phase 2 trial evaluates the safety and efficacy of PHITAH and PHIT autologous bioengineered skin grafts in basal cell carcinoma patients undergoing reconstructive surgery — a positive result would support the clinical and commercial viability of the tissue-engineered skin platform. With only 21 estimated enrollees, the trial is severely underpowered and the primary readout is not expected until 2024, limiting near-term catalysts.

This trial was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient (actual enrollment = 0), rendering it uninformative as a clinical or investment catalyst. No data will emerge from this record; any PFS signal from prior exploratory studies cannot be extrapolated to this protocol.

indication: Adenocarcinoma of the esophagus or esophagogastric junction, unresectable/chemoradiation-ineligible, palliative
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates whether palliative short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy (5 × 4 Gy) followed by platinum-based chemotherapy (oxaliplatin + fluorouracil) can meaningfully improve dysphagia in unresectable esophageal/EGJ adenocarcinoma — a supportive-care question, not a survival or curative endpoint. With only 29 patients, no comparator arm, and a dysphagia-score surrogate endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct registrational weight.

indication: Hematologic malignancies (CLL, MCL, FL, MZL, DLBCL, Richter transformation, BL)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation study establishes the MTD and recommended dose for zilovertamab vedotin (a DLL3-targeting ADC) across multiple hematologic malignancies, with the key catalyst being tolerability confirmation and any early efficacy signal in DLBCL or Richter transformation. As a completed first-in-human study, the primary investor read-through is RDR and safety profile — not registrational — and the commercial path will depend on whether a larger, randomized development is initiated.

indication: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia or Lymphoblastic Lymphoma, 1L
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates DA-EPOCH chemotherapy (etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) in ALL/LLB1, with morphologic CR and MRD response rate as co-primary endpoints — a signal-finding study rather than registrational. The absence of a comparator arm and use of response biomarkers (MRD) limit direct commercial read-through; results would be hypothesis-generating for a potential registrational combination strategy including dasatinib/imatinib. Limited investor relevance as a single-arm academic study with no OS-powered primary endpoint.

indication: Resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, neoadjuvant setting
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the PD-L1 inhibitor carrelizumab (carrelizumab) to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and apatinib (a VEGFR TKI) can achieve pathologic complete response in resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — a setting where IO has historically underperformed in this tumor type. With only 42 patients, no comparator arm, and a PCR surrogate endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating at best and would require a randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial thesis.

This study was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient (actual enrollment = 0), rendering it uninformative as a clinical or regulatory catalyst. No investable signal can be drawn from this record; the key watch item is whether ImaginAb has disclosed a reason for withdrawal (e.g., safety, strategic) that investors should be aware of.

This trial tests whether neoadjuvant sonidegib (a Hedge pathway inhibitor) can shrink BCC tumors to spare surgical scarring, with optical coherence tomography as the response readout — a surrogate, not a survival endpoint. With only 16 patients enrolled across 3 arms, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no registrational weight.

indication: Hematologic malignancies, post-non-myeloablative stem cell transplant (GVHD prophylaxis)
investor_note: This completed Phase 2 trial evaluated whether adding sirolimus (an mTOR inhibitor) to standard tacrolimus and methotrexate GVHD prophylaxis reduces the incidence and severity of GVHD in non-myeloablative transplant settings — a clinically meaningful but niche question for immunomodulatory strategies. As a completed, non-randomized academic study, results are hypothesis-generating rather than registrational, and the absence of a comparator arm limits causal inference.

This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial evaluated neoadjuvant lapatinib (HER2/EGFR TKI) plus letrozole (ER inhibitor) vs. letrozole alone in HER2-negative early breast cancer, with cOR as the key signal-finding endpoint. The trial is completed; results are historical context rather than a forward-looking catalyst, but the combination's superior response rate in the HER2-negative setting has informed neoadjuvant endocrine/TKI regimen design.

indication: HPV16+ advanced or recurrent cervical cancer, post-standard-of-care failure
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2a study evaluates the safety and ORR of VB10.16 (a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) combined with atezolizumab in HPV16+ cervical cancer patients who have already failed or are ineligible for standard of care — a high-unmet-need but difficult-to-treat population. The key catalyst is whether the combination demonstrates meaningful ORR signal in a heavily pretreated, single-arm design; the absence of a comparator arm and surrogate ORR endpoint limit direct registrational read-through.

indication: Advanced or metastatic breast cancer (HR+/HER2-) and colorectal cancer
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation and expansion study aims to establish the safety profile and optimal dose of PF-08032562 — a novel small molecule — in HR+/HER2- breast cancer and colorectal cancer, with ORR in Part 2 as the key efficacy signal. The key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any early efficacy readout in the heavily pre-treated population, though the non-randomized, open-label, multi-indication design limits the ability to draw registrational conclusions at this stage.

This completed Phase 1 study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of intravesical BCG combined with the recombinant MAGE-A3 protein (recMAGE-A3) and AS15 adjuvant in NMIBC patients, with the goal of enhancing local and systemic T cell responses. With only 23 patients enrolled and a safety/tolerability primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating, signal-finding study — not registrational — and any commercial read-through would require larger efficacy-driven trials to establish clinical utility.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
investor_note: This randomized, controlled, open-label Phase 3 trial tests SYS6002 (a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) against investigator's choice chemotherapy in urothelial carcinoma, with OS as the registrational endpoint. The key watch item is whether the bispecific's OS signal is strong enough to support a regulatory filing — the open-label design and lack of a comparator OS subgroup (vs. chemotherapy) are the principal read-through caveats.

This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2b trial evaluates whether low-dose tamoxifen citrate (an SERM) can reduce mammographic breast density and, by extension, breast cancer risk in radiation-induced cancer survivors — a population with heightened need for cancer prevention. The primary endpoint of mammographic breast density is a surrogate/surgical biomarker, not a cancer incidence or mortality measure, limiting its direct commercial relevance to investors.

This Phase 1/2 safety trial of DCVAC/PCa (a personalized cancer vaccine targeting prostate cancer antigens) combined with ONCOS-102 (an oncolytic virus) in mCRPC was terminated after enrolling only 5 patients, rendering any efficacy or safety signal non-interpretable. The termination and near-zero enrollment make this a non-actionable catalyst — investors should not draw conclusions about the combination's clinical viability from this record.

indication: HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer, receiving capivasertib + fulvestrant
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether loperamide (a GI proton pump inhibitor) and/or cetirizine (an antihistamine) can effectively reduce the incidence of grade ≥2 diarrhea and rash — two of capivasertib's most common and treatment-limiting toxicities — in HR+/HER2- breast cancer patients on capivasertib + fulvestrant. A positive result would support a prophylactic strategy to improve tolerability and, potentially, adherence to the capivasertib combination, though the open-label design, surrogate toxicity endpoints, and academic sponsorship mean the primary commercial read-through is limited.

This pilot study evaluates the safety and tolerability of the DRibble cancer vaccine (with cyclophosphamide, imiquimod, and HPV vaccinations) in just 3 men with advanced prostate cancer — a pure safety/feasibility read. With only 3 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, any signal of immune activation or tumor response is purely anecdotal and not registrational.

indication: Breast cancer with major depressive episode
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial compared citalopram (a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) vs. psychotherapy as antidepressant treatment in breast cancer patients with major depressive episode, using BDI score change as the primary endpoint. The trial was terminated with only 40 patients enrolled, severely limiting any efficacy conclusions and materially reducing its value as a commercial catalyst.

indication: Advanced non-hematologic malignancies (pancreatic, head and neck, prostatic), PET-avid
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial evaluated PF-00562271, a FAK inhibitor, establishing safety, PK, and early metabolic signal (≥15% FDG-PET tumor reduction) in PET-avid solid tumors. As a completed early-phase, non-randomized study, its investor relevance is limited to informing RP2D selection and whether FAK inhibition showed enough metabolic signal to justify further development.

indication: Extensive, limited, and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), 1L radiotherapy prevention
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial tests whether MRI surveillance alone (with no preventive cranial irradiation) improves overall survival versus MRI surveillance plus PCI in SCLC — a positive result would support a non-radiation, imaging-only prevention strategy for this indication. The key watch item is whether the OS benefit from delaying/omitting PCI is clinically meaningful and not offset by increased risk of brain metastases.

indication: Intermediate-risk squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), adjuvant
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding durvalumab (PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor) to adjuvant IMRT can improve 3-year DFS rate in intermediate-risk SCCHN — a setting where IO integration post-radiotherapy remains investigational. With only 18 patients enrolled, results are hypothesis-generating at best; the key watch is whether DFS signal is strong enough to justify a randomized trial before any regulatory or commercial read-through.

indication: Recurrent Ewing's family of tumors or desmoplastic small round-cell tumor (DSRCT)
investor_note: This completed single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated imatinib mesylate (a KIT/PDGF receptor TKI) as a salvage strategy in relapsed Ewing's sarcoma or desmoplastic small round-cell tumor, with ORR as the key signal-finding endpoint. With only 40 estimated patients, no comparator arm, and a completed status dating to 2007, this trial is of historical/scientific interest rather than an active near-term catalyst.

indication: Multiple brain metastases from solid tumors
investor_note: This completed Phase 2 Proof of Concept study evaluated the safety and immunoreceptor (131I-L19SIP) uptake of a fully human anti-angiogenic antibody combined with WBRT in patients with multiple brain metastases; the key catalyst was establishing tolerability and early signal of anti-tumor activity in the brain. With only 32 patients, a single arm, and a safety/feasibility primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating study — any commercial read-through would require larger efficacy-driven trials to support advancement.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD and safety profile of ADCLEC.syn1 CAR-T cells in relapsed/refractory AML — a high-unmet-need but historically difficult-to-treat indication. The key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any early efficacy signal at the RP2D; however, the single-arm, 40-patient design limits conclusions to safety/dose-finding only.

This randomized Phase 2 trial uses a proteomic assay to assess whether aspirin-induced acetylation of COX-1 in platelets and colonic mucosa correlates with chemopreventive activity — a mechanistic/biomarker-deconvolution question, not an efficacy readout. The key watch item is whether the proteomic biomarker of COX-1 acetylation can predict which patients benefit from aspirin, but the primary endpoint is a surrogate biomarker measure, not a cancer prevention or survival outcome.

This Phase 2 trial tests whether adding autologous αDC1 intradermal vaccines to an intensive locoregional cisplatin + CKM chemoimmunotherapy backbone improves CD8+ T-cell infiltration into the peritoneal fluid of advanced ovarian cancer patients — a mechanistic, not registrational, endpoint. The trial was terminated with only 25 estimated enrollees, severely limiting any efficacy signal and materially reducing its commercial or regulatory relevance.

indication: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma (primary tumor <5 cm), any line
investor_note: This completed Phase 1/2 trial evaluated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) as a locoregional strategy to enable or potentiate systemic therapy in small primary RCC tumors, with PFS as the signal-finding endpoint. Non-randomized, multi-arm design and academic sponsorship limit direct commercial read-through; results are hypothesis-generating for locoregional management of small RCC primaries rather than a registrational catalyst.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial establishes the MTD and safety profile of oral KPT-9274 (a PI3Kδ inhibitor) in heavily pre-treated R/R AML — the key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any early response signal to support RP2D selection. With only 16 patients enrolled across 6 dose arms, this is strictly a safety/dose-finding readout with no efficacy conclusions expected.

This first-in-human dose-escalation trial sought to establish the RP2D and safety profile of Nuc-1031 (a novel small molecule) combined with carboplatin in recurrent ovarian cancer — a high-unmet-need indication with few approved options. With only 25 patients enrolled and a safety/MTD primary endpoint, this is a pure de-risking step; any efficacy signal would be hypothesis-generating only and not registrational.

indication: Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, post-chemo with incomplete response, autologous SCT setting
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated whether adding 90Y Zevalin (a targeted radioimmunotherapy agent) to high-dose chemo + autologous SCT could improve outcomes in myeloma patients who had an incomplete response to prior induction — a setting with high unmet need. The trial was terminated with only 8 patients enrolled, severely limiting any efficacy conclusions and materially reducing its value as a commercial catalyst.

indication: Relapsed and refractory aggressive B- and T-cell lymphomas
investor_note: This Phase 1 dose-escalation study of volasertib (PLK1 inhibitor) plus belinostat (HDAC inhibitor) in relapsed/refractory aggressive lymphomas was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient, rendering it a null catalyst with no data generated. No investable signal exists; the trial's withdrawal signals programmatic halt that investors should monitor through sponsor disclosures for any rationale or pipeline reorganization.

This pilot trial characterizes the cardiac and safety profile of cytarabine and daunorubicin hydrochloride (7+3) in newly diagnosed AML, with the primary catalyst being cardiac toxicity mitigation, not efficacy. With only 40 patients, a single arm, and no comparator, this is a feasibility/safety de-risking step — not a registrational or commercially actionable signal.

This single-arm investigator-sponsored study tests whether adding the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab to the TKI lenvatinib can extend PFS in PD-L1+ EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients who have already progressed on a TKI — a setting where IO has historically underperformed in unselected patients. With only 35 estimated patients, no comparator arm, and a PFS primary endpoint, results will be hypothesis-generating at best and will require a randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial thesis.

This real-world, single-arm study evaluates whether adding methotrexate to adalimumab improves satisfactory response rates (investigator and patient-assessed) in suboptimal responders — a post-marketing effectiveness question, not a registrational catalyst. With only 46 patients, no comparator arm, and a non-standard efficacy endpoint, findings are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct regulatory weight.

This multicenter Phase 2 trial evaluates MK3475 (pazutinib, an anti-VEGFR TKI) combined with metronomic cyclophosphamide in advanced sarcomas, with 6-month ORR and non-progression rate as co-primary endpoints. The non-randomized, single-arm design and surrogate endpoints limit direct regulatory translation without a confirmatory trial.

indication: Mild and moderate hepatic impairment (non-acute liver disease)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 study characterizes the drug's pharmacokinetics (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) in patients with mild/moderate hepatic impairment versus those with normal liver function — a key prerequisite for safe dosing in this population. With only 28 patients, a single arm, and a PK-only primary endpoint, this is a regulatory bridging study, not an efficacy catalyst.

This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether a hypofractionated 8 Gy/1 targeted radiotherapy schedule is non-inferior to the standard 20 Gy/5 2026 in overall survival for poor-prognosis brain metastasis patients — a result that could reshape the current 20 Gy/5 treatment paradigm. The key watch item is whether the 8 Gy/1 schedule maintains efficacy (OS equivalence) despite a dramatically reduced dose and volume, which would support broader adoption of hypofractionated targeted radiotherapy in this high-unmet-need setting.

indication: Stage IIIa primary hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein thrombosis
investor_note: This first-in-human comparison of recombinant human adenovirus type 5 hepatic artery infusion combined with TACE in a difficult-to-treat HCC subgroup (portal vein thrombosis) aims to establish disease control rate as a proof-of-concept for the oncolytic virus + TACE combination. With only 38 estimated patients, a single arm, and an academic sponsor, this is a hypothesis-generating, signal-finding study — not a registrational catalyst.

indication: Multiple myeloma and cutaneous lymphoma (HSPC mobilization, no line specified)
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 study evaluated the safety and feasibility of adding ATRA (a vitamin A derivative) to standard G-CSF-based hematopoietic stem cell mobilization in multiple myeloma and cutaneous lymphoma patients; with only 6 patients enrolled, findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and would require a larger controlled study to establish clinical utility. The extremely small sample, single-arm design, and safety-only primary endpoint make this a signal-finding study with no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial sought to establish the clinical efficacy of combining the proteasome inhibitor bortezomib with the HDAC inhibitor vorinostat in high-risk MDS or AML, but was terminated early with only 16 patients enrolled — severely limiting any efficacy conclusions. The terminated status and single-arm design render this trial uninformative for regulatory or investment purposes.

This pilot trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy of NovoTTF-100L tumor-treating fields (TTFields) added to gemcitabine or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in untreated advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma — a historically difficult-to-treat indication with few approved options. The key catalyst is establishing tolerability and compliance with the TTFields device as a platform for a potential registrational study; the small enrollment (n=40) and pilot/feasibility design mean this is purely a safety/proof-of-concept readout, not a registrational or efficacy-defining dataset.

indication: Breast cancer with bone-dominant metastases, post-endocrine therapy
investor_note: This completed single-arm Phase 2 study evaluated the clinical effect of multiple intravenous radium-223 (Xofigo) injections on bone turnover markers (NTX, ALP) in endocrine-refractory breast cancer patients with bone-dominant metastases — a setting where the radiopharmaceutical has not been approved. With only 23 patients, no comparator arm, and a surrogate/biomarker endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating at best and would require a randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial claim.

This single-arm academic study evaluates whether the 68Ga-DOTATATE PET scan — a novel imaging modality — can change clinical management and patient outcomes versus conventional imaging in neuroendocrine carcinoma, with patient-care impact as the primary endpoint. The absence of a comparator arm and use of a care-plan-change (a functional, non-validated endpoint) limit direct commercial or regulatory relevance; findings are hypothesis-generating for PET scan adoption rather than a basis for approval.

indication: Advanced or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma, ≥65 years
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial directly compares oral cyclophosphamide vs. doxorubicin in elderly (≥65 years) advanced/metastatic STS patients, with PFS as the primary endpoint — a result that could reshape standard-of-care and support oral chemotherapy adoption in this population. The key watch item is whether oral cyclophosphamide demonstrates a superior PFS profile and tolerability that justifies a label or prescribing preference over doxorubicin in elderly STS patients.

This investigator-sponsored Phase 1/2 trial evaluates the MTD and ORR of a novel FLT3 inhibitor (ASTX727) combined with venetoclax and gilteritinib in FLT3-mutated AML/high-risk MDS, testing whether the triplet can deliver meaningful signal-finding activity in a difficult-to-treat population. The single-arm, non-randomized design and academic sponsorship limit direct commercial read-through; watch for early efficacy signals and RP2D confirmation before any registrational conclusions can be drawn.

indication: HER2+ metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer, unoperable
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 study evaluated the laboratory biomarker effects (platelet function, thrombokinetic changes) of trastuzumab emtansine (T-DXd) in a heavily biomarker-restricted HER2+ breast cancer population; it is purely exploratory and hypothesis-generating for the PK/dose-finding question, not registrational. With only 13 patients enrolled and a single-arm design, findings are signal-finding only and would require a larger controlled study to support any commercial thesis.

indication: Hematological cancers (leukemia, MDS, MDS/MPN), mixed lines
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 2 trial evaluated allogeneic bone marrow transplant with busulfan, fludarabine, and antithymocyte globulin conditioning, assessing treatment-related mortality and engraftment as key indicators. As a completed, non-randomized academic study, results are hypothesis-generating rather than registrational, and the absence of a comparator arm limits causal inference on the conditioning regimen's efficacy.

This single-arm Phase 2 study tests whether adding the PD-1/CTLA-4 inhibitor QL1706 (Du Juan) to a lenvatinib + AG (likely anti-CTLA-4 + GM-CSF) backbone can improve mPFS in treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic cancer — a hard-to-treat indication with few approved options. The absence of a comparator arm and use of mPFS (a surrogate, not OS) limit the strength of any efficacy signal; watch for single-arm run-in data and whether the regimen can differentiate from standard lenvatinib monotherapy in this setting.

This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation study sought to establish the safety profile and MTD of imetelstat (GRN163L), a splice-targeting agent, in heavily pre-treated myeloma patients — the key catalyst was tolerability confirmation and any early efficacy signal to support RP2D selection. With only 20 patients enrolled and a safety/MTD primary endpoint, this is purely a dose-finding and risk-characterization read; no registrational conclusions can be drawn from this study alone.

indication: Recurrent or refractory childhood solid tumors
investor_note: This completed Phase 2 trial evaluated the combination of thalidomide (an anti-angiogenic small molecule) and cyclophosphamide in relapsed/refractory pediatric solid tumors, aiming to establish antitumor activity of the combination. No primary outcome measures are recorded in the registry entry, limiting retrospective assessment of the trial's efficacy signal.

indication: Extremity recurrent malignant soft tissue sarcoma
investor_note: This randomized surgical trial compares barrier resection vs. local wide resection in extremity-recurrent soft tissue sarcoma, with local recurrence rate as the primary endpoint — a functional/structural question rather than a drug efficacy question. The trial's UNKNOWN status, estimated (not actual) enrollment, and academic sponsorship limit commercial read-through; it is primarily relevant for surgical oncology practice guidelines rather than as a direct investment catalyst.

This investigator-sponsored, non-randomized study evaluates QL1706 (a PD-L1/CTLA-4 bispecific) combined with nab-paclitaxel ± bevacizumab as 1L therapy in r/mTNBC, with ORR as the key signal-generating endpoint. The non-randomized, single-arm design and surrogate ORR endpoint limit direct regulatory or commercial read-through; results would be hypothesis-generating for the QL1706 combination strategy in a high-unmet-need indication.

indication: Relapsed or refractory indolent B-cell lymphoma (follicular lymphoma, marginal lymphoma)
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial evaluated bortezomib (Velcade) combined with rituximab in relapsed/refractory indolent B-cell lymphoma, with time-to-progression as the primary endpoint. No primary outcomes were pre-specified in the record, limiting the ability to assess the precise efficacy signal; the trial is completed and the key historical readout is time-to-progression data from the published literature.

This Phase 1 dose-escalation study of ASP1951 (a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) alone and combined with pembrolizumab was terminated before completion, materially limiting any safety or RP2D conclusions. The termination is the dominant investor signal — the program did not advance to Phase 2.

indication: CML (dasatinib/nilotinib-resistant) and Ph+ ALL (post-TKI failure), Japanese patients
investor_note: This Japan-specific Phase 1/2 study evaluated ponatinib (a BCR-ABL TKI) in two heavily pre-treated CML/Ph+ ALL populations where prior TKI failure left no effective option; the Phase 1 DLT/RP2D and Phase 2 MCyR/MaHR signals would support dose and indication selection for regional approval. With only 35 patients, a non-randomized single-arm design, and a 2018 primary completion, this is a historical Japanese bridging study — not a registrational catalyst.

indication: Unspecified solid tumors (chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy prevention)
investor_note: This completed Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trial evaluated whether vitamin E supplementation could reduce the incidence of chemotherapy-induced sensory peripheral neuropathy (≥Grade 2) in solid tumor patients — a supportive-care question, not a drug-approval catalyst. With an open-label design, a surrogate neuropathy endpoint, and a non-drug intervention, this trial holds minimal direct investment relevance for oncology drug developers.

indication: Breast, GI, and gynecologic cancer (chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy)
investor_note: This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial sought to evaluate whether topical menthol reduces neuropathic pain (BPI-SF worst pain score) in cancer patients on taxane/platinum chemotherapy, but was terminated with only 12 patients enrolled — far below any meaningful efficacy threshold. The trial's early termination and minimal accrual render it uninvestable; any data generated would be hypothesis-generating at best.

indication: Glioblastoma multiforme or other brain tumors (GBM, gliosarcoma)
investor_note: This NCI-sponsored pilot trial evaluated the optimal dose and efficacy of erlotinib (EGFR TKI) combined with the chemotherapy temozolomide and radiation in GBM — a historically difficult-to-treat indication. As a completed single-arm Phase 2, results are historical and primarily hypothesis-generating; the key investor watch is whether erlotinib's radiation-sensitizing mechanism demonstrated sufficient OS signal to justify further development in this niche.

This completed single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated a gemcitabine/capecitabine/sorafenib triplet in unresectable RCC, with PFS as the primary signal-finding endpoint. With only 40 estimated patients, no comparator arm, and a now largely discontinued sorafenib combination, this trial holds minimal direct investment relevance.

indication: Advanced NSCLC, elderly or ECOG 2 patients, 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial sought to establish whether adding erlotinib (Tarceva) to gemcitabine at progression could improve PFS in elderly/ECOG-2 advanced NSCLC patients, but the trial was terminated before completion — materially limiting any efficacy conclusions. The termination is the dominant investor signal; any interim data should be interpreted with caution given the early discontinuation and non-survival primary endpoint.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC (EGFR TKI-targeted), Chinese patients
investor_note: This Phase 4 PK/absorption study compares gefitinib CTTQ (a generic) against Iressa (osimertinib) in Chinese NSCLC patients, with the goal of establishing bioavailability and drug-level equivalence to support local regulatory approval, not demonstrating efficacy. The primary readout is pharmacokinetic profiling (C, Tmax, AUC, t½), not survival or response — this is a regulatory bridging study, not a registrational trial.

indication: Advanced cancer with intractable pain, delirium, dyspnea, or nausea
investor_note: This pilot study aimed to determine whether dexmedetomidine could serve as a sedation alternative to midazolam in advanced cancer patients with refractory symptoms, with a Phase 3 trial as the next step. The study was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient (actual enrollment = 0), rendering it uninformative for any investment thesis.

This first-in-human dose-escalation and cohort-expansion study aims to establish the MTD and early efficacy signal in selected solid tumor indications for MPB-1734; the key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any RP2D selection that could support indication prioritization. As a single-arm, uncontrolled Phase 1/2 study, results are hypothesis-generating only and carry substantial early-phase risk.

indication: HPV-associated (p16+) oropharynx squamous cell carcinoma, T0-3N0-2, post-operative
investor_note: This single-institution study uses ctDNA risk stratification to de-escalate cisplatin-based post-operative therapy in p16+ oropharynx cancer, aiming to spare patients from overtreatment while preserving 2-year PFS in the high-risk cohort. With only 50 patients, no comparator arm, and a surrogate endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating at best and would require a larger randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial pathway.

This feasibility study tests whether CivaTech's LDR brachytherapy device — a permanently implantable Pd-103 electrode (CivaSheet) — achieves acceptable 1-year local control rates in resected early-stage lung cancer, with the key catalyst being proof of clinical safety and signal for the larger registrational trial. With only 40 patients, a single arm, and a 1-year local control primary endpoint, this is a device/feasibility read, not a registrational or efficacy-defining event.

This Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety and tolerability of chemoradiation followed by dostarlimab (PD-1 inhibitor) maintenance in node-positive Stage IIIC endometrial cancer, with the key catalyst being whether the IO component can be safely added to a platinum-based chemoradiation backbone. With only 21 estimated enrollees, this is a hypothesis-generating safety study — any signal of tolerability and early anti-tumor activity in this biomarker-restricted population would be the critical readout to watch.

indication: Angiomyolipoma (Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and sporadic LAM)
investor_note: This completed long-term follow-up study assessed the sustained tolerability and biological activity (angiomyolipoma regression) of everolimus (RAD001) in TSC and sporadic LAM patients previously enrolled in a prior Phase 1/2 trial. With only 20 patients and a tolerability primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating, not registrational, study — any commercial read-through would require a larger efficacy-driven trial to support label claims.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding cetuximab (EGFR inhibitor) to conformal thoracic radiotherapy, followed by docetaxel + cetuximab, can extend PFS in unresectable LA-NSCLC — a setting where EGFR targeting has biological rationale but clinical evidence remains limited. With only 27 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, results are hypothesis-generating at best and would require a randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial claim.

indication: Poor-risk acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) or bilineage/biphenotypic leukemia, relapsed/refractory
investor_note: This completed NCI-sponsored Phase 1 dose-escalation trial sought to establish the MTD and tolerability of an HDAC inhibitor (entinostat) combined with clofarabine in high-risk ALL — a setting where a tolerable, efficacy-boosting regimen would be hypothesis-generating for future studies. With only 27 patients enrolled and a purely safety/MTD primary endpoint, this is a dose-finding signal at best, not an efficacy-defining catalyst.

This randomized Phase 1/2 trial evaluates the safety and efficacy of interstitial oncolysis (IRE) surgery combined with γδ T cell therapy in locally advanced pancreatic cancer, with PFS and OS as co-primary endpoints. The trial is completed and academic-sponsored, limiting direct commercial read-through; results would be hypothesis-generating for the IRE + γδ T cell combination in a difficult-to-treat solid tumor.

This randomized Phase 1 trial evaluates the optimal dose and postoperative analgesic effect of oxycodone combined with ultrasound-guided paravertebral nerve block in thoracoscopic lung cancer surgery, with NRS pain scores at rest and cough as the primary endpoint. The key watch item is whether a safe and effective dose of oxycodone can be established to support multimodal analgesia in this surgical setting — but the academic sponsorship, open-label design, and pain-score surrogate limit direct commercial read-through.

This randomized Phase 3 trial tests whether adding thalidomide maintenance therapy to standard R-CHOP treatment improves relapse-free survival in DLBCL — a historically difficult-to-treat indication. The key watch item is whether the maintenance strategy meaningfully shifts the relapse-free survival curve; the open-label design and use of a relapse-free (not OS) primary endpoint are the principal read-through caveats.

indication: Advanced solid tumors, NSCLC, melanoma, SCCHN, TNBC, adrenocortical carcinoma, mesothelioma, and MDCs (all Phase 1 dose-escalation cohorts)
investor_note: This multi-part dose-escalation study evaluates eganelisib (IPI-549), a PI3Kα/δ inhibitor, as monotherapy and in combination with nivolumab across a broad basket of advanced solid tumors and immunomodulatory cell populations; the key catalyst is establishing a tolerable RP2D and any early signal of immune activation in the IO combination. As a Phase 1 basket study with no randomized comparator, this is purely a safety/dose-finding step — registrational conclusions cannot be drawn from this design.

indication: Stage I/II adenocarcinoma of the prostate, neoadjuvant chemoprevention
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 2 randomized trial evaluated soy isoflavone regimens as neoadjuvant chemoprevention prior to radical prostatectomy, using biomarkers of oxidative DNA damage (5-HMR) and lipid peroxidation (8-isoprostane) as surrogate endpoints. With only 32 patients enrolled and a biomarker-focused design, findings are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct registrational weight.

This exploratory study tests whether a pedometer/actigraph-based "prescribed" exercise program can improve balance confidence (ABC Scale) in cancer patients at high risk of injurious falls — a functional, not oncologic, endpoint. With only 34 patients, no comparator arm, and a non-oncologic primary endpoint, this is a feasibility/d feasibility-of-approach study with no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst.

indication: EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC, post-EGFR TKI progression
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 study characterised the PK profile of AZD9291 (osimertinib) and its metabolites (AZ5104, AZ7550) in Chinese EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients who had already progressed on a prior EGFR TKI, serving as a foundational safety/PK de-risking step for osimertinib's development program. As a completed PK/dose-finding study, its investor relevance is limited to informing regional regulatory submissions rather than generating efficacy signal.

indication: EGFR-mutant stage IB-IIIB non-squamous NSCLC, adjuvant (MRD+)
investor_note: This multicenter, non-randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether MRD positivity should trigger adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy to improve 3-year DFS rate in resected EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC — a biomarker-driven question with implications for the EGFR-TKI class. Key caveats are the non-randomized, single-arm design with a surrogate DFS endpoint, limiting direct inferability of a causal benefit without a comparator arm.

This completed single-arm study assessed whether the omega-3 supplement Lovaza™ (4g/day) modulates breast cancer risk biomarkers in premenopausal women — a mechanistic/biomarker question, not an efficacy or survival readout. With only 36 subjects, no comparator arm, and a non-standard primary endpoint, findings are hypothesis-generating at best and carry no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst.

This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether genomic profiling can identify actionable targets to guide metastatic breast cancer therapy — comparing targeted treatment based on molecular alterations vs. standard maintenance chemotherapy (targeted substudy) and vs. vandetanib/selumetinib as maintenance in the IO-eligible (no actionable genomics) arm. A PFS win in either substudy would validate genomic-guided treatment selection as a clinical decision tool, though the open-label design, PFS-only primary endpoint, and cooperative-group sponsorship limit direct regulatory/regulatory-bridging impact.

indication: Intraductal carcinoma (DCIS), occult invasive breast cancer detection
investor_note: This single-arm feasibility study tests whether FAPI-PET/MRI with [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 can detect occult invasive cancer in surgical DCIS specimens — a diagnostic/imaging rather than therapeutic catalyst. With only 30 patients, no comparator arm, and a feasibility primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating study with no near-term commercial read-through.

indication: Chronic non-cancer pain (opioid-tolerant patients, primary care setting)
investor_note: This pilot study evaluates ultra-low dose oral ketamine as an analgesic and opioid-sparing agent in opioid-tolerant primary care patients with chronic non-cancer pain, using patient-reported outcome scales (BPI) as co-primary endpoints. With only 32 estimated enrollees, an UNKNOWN status, and a primary completion date already passed (H1 2015), this trial is likely underpowered and its results would be hypothesis-generating at best — not a registrational catalyst.

This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation trial established the MTD and recommended Phase 2 dose for sorafenib combined with FOLFIRI in first-line metastatic colorectal cancer; the key output is an RP2D to carry into subsequent efficacy studies. With only 16 patients enrolled and a single-arm design, this is purely a safety/dose-finding exercise — any efficacy signal would be hypothesis-generating only.

indication: HR+ HER2- metastatic breast cancer with visceral metastasis, 1L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial tests whether adding the CDK4/6 inhibitor ribociclib to standard endocrine therapy or chemotherapy (± bevacizumab) improves PFS in first-line HR+ HER2- metastatic breast cancer with visceral metastasis. With only 41 patients enrolled, the study is severely underpowered and results will be hypothesis-generating at best — not a registrational catalyst.

This terminated Phase 2 trial sought to assess docetaxel's complete response rate (serum PSA <0.2 ng/mL) in just 3 patients with relapsed prostate cancer — far too few to generate meaningful efficacy conclusions. With terminated status, near-zero enrollment, and no comparator arm, this trial holds no near-term catalyst value.

This randomized Phase 3 trial evaluates romiplostim (a thrombopoietin receptor agonist) for managing chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia in pediatric/adolescent solid malignancy patients, with hematologic response at 12 weeks as the primary endpoint. With only 30 estimated enrollees, an academic sponsor, and a surrogate/hematologic endpoint, this is a small, investigator-sponsored study with limited near-term commercial catalyst value.

indication: Occult ovarian cancer (FRA+ tumors), surgical staging
investor_note: This completed academic Phase 1 trial evaluated whether EC17 (a fluorescent dye) could detect fallopian tube cancer (FRA+) tumors during surgery — a diagnostic/imaging feasibility question, not a therapeutic efficacy readout. With only 10 patients and no comparator arm, results are purely exploratory and would need validation in a larger study before any commercial relevance can be drawn.

This completed NCI-sponsored Phase 1/2 trial sought to establish the MTD and early efficacy signal for cilengitide (an anti-angiogenic small molecule) combined with the standard temozolomide + radiation backbone in newly diagnosed GBM. The trial is now completed and its historical readout is primarily of scientific/academic interest — any OS signal would have supported further development of the cilengitide combination, but the subsequent Phase 3 trial of this regimen failed, rendering the program defunct.

This randomized Phase 2 trial compares two flumatinib doses (400–600 mg) against imatinib 400 mg in newly diagnosed Ph+ CML-CP, with MMR rate at 6 months as the key efficacy signal. The open-label, multi-center design and surrogate endpoint (MMR rather than OS) are the primary read-through caveats, though the unknown status and estimated primary completion date of June 2012 raise concerns about whether results have been reported.

This first-in-human study evaluates the safety and manufacturability of CD22-directed CAR-T cells in a heavily pre-treated, CD22+ relapsed/refractory leukemia population — a novel antigen-escape strategy from CD19-directed therapy. With only 4 patients enrolled, this is a pure safety/feasibility read; any efficacy signal would be hypothesis-generating only.

This academic feasibility/proof-of-concept study evaluates whether advanced MRI perfusion techniques (DSWI-CEMR) can predict treatment response (local progression-free time) after gamma-knife radiosurgery — not to generate efficacy evidence. With only 23 patients, a single arm, and a non-standard primary endpoint, this is purely hypothesis-generating and has no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst value.

This investigator-sponsored, single-arm study tests whether intratumoral Vusolimogene Oderparepvec (VO) — a TROP2-directed oncolytic virus — can generate an objective response in IO-refractory angiosarcoma when combined with pembrolizumab, a PD-1 inhibitor. With only 18 estimated patients and no comparator arm, any signal would be hypothesis-generating only and insufficient to support registration without larger controlled follow-on studies.

This first-in-human neoadjuvant study tests whether ipilimumab (CTLA-4 checkpoint blockade) can be safely and feasibly delivered prior to standard surgery/chemoradiation in newly diagnosed GBM, with OS and ORR as secondary signals to watch. With only 16 patients and no comparator arm, this is a pure safety/feasibility read — not registrational — and any efficacy signal would be hypothesis-generating only.

This Phase 1b/2 study of rociletinib (EGFR TKI) plus MPDL3280A (VEGFR TKI) in EGFR-mutant NSCLC was terminated after enrolling only 3 patients, rendering any safety or efficacy signal non-interpretable. The termination with near-zero enrollment is a critical negative signal for the combination program and warrants close scrutiny of the underlying rationale (e.g., futility, safety concerns) before drawing conclusions.

indication: Resectable or potentially resectable Stage III NSCLC, neoadjuvant
investor_note: This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the BTLA inhibitor JS004 to a PD-1 antibody (toripalimab) plus platinum-based chemotherapy backbone improves pathologic complete response rates in resectable Stage III NSCLC — a setting where achieving PCR is associated with better survival. The key watch item is whether the BTLA blockade combination can meaningfully outperform the IO-chemo backbone; the open-label design and PCR-only primary endpoint (no OS) temper the strength of any efficacy signal.

indication: NY-ESO-1+ multiple myeloma, melanoma, synovial sarcoma, myxoid/round cell liposarcoma (HLA-A*0201 restricted)
investor_note: This first-in-human trial sought to establish the safety and manufacturing feasibility of CRISPR-engineered NY-ESO-1 redirected autologous T cells (NYCE T cells) across multiple tumor types, but was terminated after enrolling only 3 patients — severely limiting any safety or efficacy signal. The terminated status and minimal enrollment render this a non-actionable catalyst; investors should not draw conclusions about the platform's clinical viability from this record.

indication: Secondary malignant neoplasm of brain and cerebral meninges (post-radiotherapy)
investor_note: This single-arm study evaluates whether 18F-fluciclovine PET/CT can accurately distinguish radiation necrosis from tumor progression on MRI — a diagnostic dilemma with no validated standard. With only 18 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, results are strictly hypothesis-generating and would need validation in a larger, controlled imaging study before any regulatory or commercial relevance can be drawn.

This single-arm academic study evaluated lithium carbonate (a non-standard, low-cost agent) as a tumor response strategy in medullary thyroid cancer, but was terminated after enrolling only 5 patients — far below any meaningful efficacy threshold. With no comparator, a terminated status, and an actual enrollment of 5, this trial carries no investable catalyst value.

This investigator-sponsored, single-arm study tests whether alpelisib (PI3Kα inhibitor) combined with capecitabine can generate tolerable doses and meaningful PFS signal in PIK3CA-mutant mCRC patients who have already progressed on two prior standard chemotherapy regimens — a setting with high unmet need and few approved options. The key watch item is whether the PFS signal is strong enough to justify a randomized, adequately powered trial; the single-arm, non-randomized design and surrogate PFS endpoint limit direct regulatory translation without further confirmatory data.

This single-arm Phase 2 study evaluates neoadjuvant RC48 (a HER2-targeting antibody) combined with carboplatin in HER2-expressing advanced ovarian cancer, with complete resection rate as the key efficacy signal. With only 47 patients, no comparator arm, and a surgical/病理 endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating at best and would require a randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial pathway.

This registrational, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial tests AL8326 — a novel small molecule — in SCLC patients who have already progressed on at least two prior chemotherapy regimens, a heavily pre-treated population where new agents are needed. A positive OS signal would support a registration pathway, but the open-label design, placebo-controlled setup, and SCLC's historically poor prognosis are key read-through caveats.

indication: Leukemia (AML, ALL, ATL, CML-BP, CLL, MDS, CMML)
investor_note: This Phase 1 dose-escalation study of terameprocol (EM-1421) sought to establish the MTD, DLT profile, and PK of an investigational agent across multiple leukemia subtypes, but was terminated before completion — materially limiting any signal interpretation. With only 16 patients enrolled, a terminated status, and no comparator, this trial carries no near-term catalyst value.

indication: metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), Stage IVB
investor_note: This Phase 1 trial evaluates whether cyclic (bipolar) androgen therapy — testosterone upcycles from castration levels to supraphysiological levels — can restore androgen receptor sensitivity and suppress PSA in mCRPC, potentially delaying progression. With only 14 estimated patients, a single arm, and a surrogate biomarker endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating feasibility study with no near-term registrational implications.

This completed Phase 1 trial evaluated the safety and immune-priming activity of an autologous dendritic cell vaccine loaded with a mixture of apoptotic/necrotic melanoma cells across multiple disease stages. With only 16 patients, no comparator, and a safety/immune-response primary endpoint, this is a hypothesis-generating and dose-finding study — not a registrational catalyst.

indication: Resectable squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), 1L
investor_note: This window-of-opportunity study tests whether short-course preoperative atezolizumab (PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor) is feasible and safe in resectable SCCHN, with translational immune-fingerprinting as a secondary signal to predict response. With only 20 patients and no comparator arm, results are hypothesis-generating at best — the key watch is whether the immune-priming signal (TILs) correlates with or can predict a meaningful clinical benefit in the subsequent adjuvant or neoadjuvant setting.

indication: AML or MDS in complete remission (CR), elderly patients (≥65y), transplant-ineligible
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates a novel FLAT (fludarabine + ARA-C + treosulfan) consolidation regimen with autologous PBSCT in transplant-ineligible elderly AML/MDS patients in CR, with 2-year DFS as the key signal. With only 15 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, results are hypothesis-generating at best and carry substantial risk of being underpowered to draw definitive efficacy conclusions.

This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the proteasome inhibitor ixazomib and the anti-CD38 antibody daratumumab to standard lenalidomide-based induction improves PFS in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed myeloma patients, with maintenance lenalidomide as the backbone. The key watch item is whether the quadruplet induction arm achieves a compelling PFS signal that could support a registrational combination strategy, though the open-label design, surrogate PFS endpoint, and non-OS primary are the principal read-through caveats.

indication: ER+/HER2- early breast cancer (Stage I-III), endocrine therapy-related musculoskeletal pain
investor_note: This pragmatic 3-arm trial tests whether duloxetine (a serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor) or furosemide (a diuretic) added to standard endocrine therapy improves musculoskeletal pain and, by extension, quality of life in ER+/HER2- early breast cancer patients — a supportive-care question with no direct drug-approval catalyst. The open-label, non-randomized design and QoL-focused primary endpoint limit its registrational or near-term commercial impact.

This randomized Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the CCR5 inhibitor vicriviroc (MK-7690) to pembrolizumab can enhance ORR in MSS-CRC — a historically IO-resistant population where no approved targeted option exists. The key watch item is whether the combination demonstrates a clinically meaningful signal in ORR that could support advancement to a registrational study; the open-label design and MSS-CRC restriction are the principal read-through caveats.

This completed Phase 1 study assessed the cardiac safety profile of ridaforolimus (an mTOR inhibitor) by measuring QTc interval prolongation following a single high dose and repeat dosing at the therapeutic level in advanced cancer patients. With only 23 participants, a single arm, and a completed status dating to 2009, this is a historical safety/MTD-defining study — not a registrational or efficacy-generating catalyst.

This pilot study of PAC-1 (a PD-1 inhibitor) combined with nivolumab was withdrawn before enrolling a single patient, rendering any efficacy signal moot. No investable catalyst exists; the trial's withdrawal with zero actual enrollment makes it a dead end unless a successor study is initiated.

This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation/identification study evaluated the safety and optimal dose of olaratumab (a PD-L1 inhibitor) as monotherapy and in combination with standard chemotherapy in pediatric patients with relapsed/refractory solid tumors. As a completed early-phase safety study, its investor relevance is limited to informing whether olaratumab advanced into later-stage development in pediatrics — the key watch is whether a tolerable dose was established to support pediatric combination regimens.

indication: HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (PI3K-activated subset)
investor_note: This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 trial tested whether adding the PI3K inhibitor BKM120 (verumab) to weekly paclitaxel improves PFS in HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with a focus on the PI3K-activated biomarker subset — a mechanistic proof-of-concept for PI3K pathway inhibition in this setting. The trial is completed; PFS as the primary endpoint is the key efficacy signal to watch, and the open-label, surrogate-endpoint design limit direct regulatory translation without a confirmatory OS study.

This completed Phase 3 randomized trial tested whether anastrozole (a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor) could reduce the incidence of histologically confirmed breast cancer in high-risk postmenopausal women — a chemoprevention endpoint with no OS/PFS follow-on. The trial is fully enrolled and completed, so the key investor read is whether the breast cancer reduction was sufficiently powered to support a label or guideline recommendation for chemoprevention use of anastrozole in this population.

indication: Progressive or relapsing pigmented villo-nodular synovitis / tenosynovial giant cell tumour (PVNS/TGCT), post-surgery
investor_note: This single-arm Phase 2 study evaluates nilotinib (a BCR-ABL TKI) as a disease-controlling strategy in a rare, surgically intractable synovial malignancy — non-progression rate at 12 weeks is the key signal. The absence of a comparator arm, surrogate endpoint, and small enrollment (50 patients) limit direct efficacy conclusions; results are hypothesis-generating for nilotinib's activity in PVNS/TGCT specifically.

This randomized Phase 3 trial tests whether adding bevacizumab (anti-VEGF mAb) to standard perioperative chemotherapy improves pCR rates in nonmetastatic breast cancer, with cardiac and perioperative complications as key safety considerations. The primary endpoint is pCR (tumor and lymph nodes), a surrogate for long-term outcomes, and the UNKNOWN status introduces uncertainty about whether the trial completed as planned.

This feasibility/proof-of-concept study tests whether SGM-101 near-infrared fluorescence-guided surgery can reliably identify and localize colorectal lung metastases intraoperatively — a diagnostic/imaging feasibility question, not a therapeutic efficacy readout. With only 10 estimated patients, a single arm, and a non-clinical primary endpoint, this is a very early-stage, signal-generating study with no direct registrational or near-term commercial catalyst value.

indication: Advanced solid tumors (breast, head and neck, NSCLC, prostate, gastric/GEJ)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD and RP2D of OCT-598 as monotherapy and in combination with docetaxel across multiple solid tumor types; the key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any early efficacy signal to support Phase 2 advancement. As a Phase 1 safety/MTD study, this is purely a de-risking step — registrational conclusions cannot be drawn from this design.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluates the PD-1 inhibitor toripalimab combined with S1 (a gut-derived growth factor) and albumin Paclitaxel as 1L therapy in advanced biliary tract cancer, with ORR as the key signal-generating endpoint. With only 30 estimated patients, no comparator arm, and an UNKNOWN status, the trial is hypothesis-generating at best and carries significant execution and regulatory risk.

indication: Progressive metastatic androgen-independent adenocarcinoma of the prostate
investor_note: This completed Phase 2 trial evaluated lutetium Lu 177-labeled monoclonal antibody J591 (a PSMA-targeted radiolabeled antibody) in castration-resistant prostate cancer, with PSA response at 8 weeks as the key signal. PSA is a surrogate endpoint and the single-arm, non-randomized design limits direct efficacy conclusions; results are hypothesis-generating for the Lu 177-PSMA combination now being tested in registrational trials.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether combining oncolytic virus Tavo (oncolytic poxvirus) delivered intratumorally via electroporation (OncoSec device) with nivolumab IV can achieve pathologic complete response in resectable advanced melanoma — a setting where pCR is associated with improved survival. With only 17 patients enrolled and no comparator arm, results are hypothesis-generating at best; the key watch is whether the combination's pCR rate meaningfully exceeds historical benchmarks for IO-primed melanoma neoadjuvant regimens.

This first-in-human dose-escalation study evaluates the safety and tolerability of αPD1-MSLN-CAR T cells — a dual-targeting CAR-T designed to simultaneously deliver PD-1 blockade via secreted nanobodies while targeting MSLN — in just 10 estimated patients across NSCLC and mesothelioma. The key catalyst is DLT/MTD definition and any early efficacy signal; with only 10 patients, this is a pure safety de-risking step with no registrational value on its own.

indication: Solid tumors (sarcoma, melanoma, SCCHN, breast, cervical, vulvar, penile, anal) — unselected, broad tumor-agnostic
investor_note: This completed Phase 1 dose-escalation study evaluates the safety, tolerability, and PK of Stimotimagene copolymerplasmid (a TLR9-activated oncolytic plasmid) across multiple solid tumor types; the key catalyst is establishing a safe and tolerable dose for the TLR9-activated oncolytic plasmid in a broad tumor-agnostic population. With only 21 patients enrolled across 3 non-randomized arms, this is strictly a safety/MTD-finding study — any efficacy signal would be purely exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

This completed Phase 1/2 trial sought to establish the MTD and then assess ORR for temozolomide combined with pazopanib hydrochloride in unresectable PNET — a rare, historically treatment-resistant tumor type. With only 29 patients enrolled and a non-randomized design, results are hypothesis-generating rather than registrational, and the ORR signal would need validation in a larger controlled study to be commercially meaningful.

indication: Relapsed or refractory solid tumors or lymphoma (pediatric, multiple histologies)
investor_note: This completed NCI-sponsored Phase 1 dose-escalation trial established the MTD and tolerability profile of ispinesib (a tubulin-targeting small molecule) in a broad pediatric tumor population; with only 30 patients enrolled across multiple histologies, findings are hypothesis-generating at best. No efficacy signal should be extrapolated; the trial is primarily a safety/dose-finding exercise with no comparator arm.

This single-arm academic study evaluates zanubrutinib (BTK inhibitor) combined with G-CVP (cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone) in 1L FL, with CRR as the key efficacy signal and MRD-guided maintenance as the stratification lens. With only 40 patients, no comparator arm, and a surrogate endpoint, results are hypothesis-generating only and would require a randomized trial to support any regulatory or commercial pathway.

This completed Phase 1 safety/tolerability study evaluated FP-1039, a novel biologic, in advanced cancer patients to establish a safe dose and tolerability profile. As a completed early-phase, single-arm study, its investor relevance is limited to informing whether FP-1039 advanced into efficacy-focused development.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma, ≥2L
investor_note: This randomized Phase 3 trial sought to establish the MTD of trabectedin (YONDALIS) in Chinese sarcoma patients previously exposed to anthracycline-based regimens, followed by an OS comparison against dacarbazine in a Part 2 expansion — a registrational-grade design if OS superiority was demonstrated. With only 16 patients enrolled in Part 1 and 16 in Part 2, the trial is severely underpowered and results are hypothesis-generating at best, not practice-changing.

This investigator-sponsored pediatric study evaluates lorlatinib (a dual ALK/ROS1 inhibitor) as monotherapy and in combination with chemotherapy in treatment-naive high-grade glioma driven by ALK or ROS1 fusions — a biomarker-selected niche with no approved targeted option in this indication. With only 15 estimated enrollees across 4 non-randomized arms, results will be hypothesis-generating at best; the key watch is disease control rate and tolerability signal that could justify a larger pediatric study.

indication: Advanced renal cell carcinoma, gastrointestinal stromal tumors, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
investor_note: This Phase 1 dose-escalation study sought to establish the MTD and DLTs of TH-302 (a PI3Kα inhibitor) combined with sunitinib across three tumor types, with Phase 2 expansion intended to generate efficacy signals at RP2D. The trial carries significant risk: single-arm, non-randomized design, early-phase status, an UNKNOWN current status, and an estimated primary completion date that has long passed with no confirmed catalyst.

indication: Head and neck cancer (oral mucositis prevention, radiation therapy)
investor_note: This NCI-sponsored Phase 3 randomized trial tests whether iseganan HCl oral solution can prevent or reduce oral mucositis in head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy — a supportive-care question, not a drug-approval catalyst. With no primary completion date, unknown status, and no enrollment figures reported, the trial offers minimal near-term investor visibility.

This single-arm Phase 2 trial tests whether adding the PD-1 inhibitor adebrelimab (SHR-1316) and low-dose bevacizumab to a TACE → HAIC chemo backbone can generate meaningful ORR and PFS signal in first-line unresectable HCC. With only 38 patients, no comparator arm, and ORR/PFS as co-primary endpoints, results will be hypothesis-generating at best — the key watch is whether the combination demonstrates a durable response that could justify a randomized trial.

This completed Phase 1 study established the safety, tolerability, and PK profile of EXS21546 — a novel small molecule from Exscientia AI — across single and multiple ascending doses in healthy male volunteers, with a Part 3 comparator study evaluating bioavailability of oral solid vs. powder formulations. The key catalyst is whether the solid formulation offers a more convenient, exequated delivery pathway that could support broader development or partner acquisition.

This randomized Phase 3 trial compared paclitaxel ± bevacizumab and paclitaxel ± capecitabine in metastatic breast cancer, with PFS as the key signal. The trial was terminated before completion, materially undermining any efficacy conclusions and rendering the dataset non-actionable for regulatory or partnering purposes.

indication: Relapsed/refractory locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (including TNBC)
investor_note: This first-in-human dose-escalation study aims to establish the MTD and tolerability of OTS167, a MELK inhibitor, in heavily pre-treated breast cancer patients — the key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any early efficacy signal to support RP2D selection. As a single-arm Phase 1 in a rare, historically treatment-resistant indication, this is purely a safety/dose-finding step with no registrational read-through.

This first-in-human study evaluates the safety and feasibility of a DLL3-targeted CAR-T in brain tumors, with efficacy signals (ORR, DIPG resection) as secondary endpoints. The key catalyst is tolerability confirmation and any early CAR-T persistence data in the immunologically cold tumor microenvironment — but the small single-arm design and novel target antigen limit near-term commercial read-through.

indication: Gastric cancer, postoperative (middle-aged and elderly patients)
investor_note: This randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluates whether adding dexmedetomidine (a sedative/analgesic) to standard care improves postoperative sleep time in gastric cancer patients aged ≥55 — a supportive-care question, not a drug-approval catalyst. With only 50 estimated enrollees, an UNKNOWN status, and a primary completion date that has already passed, the trial is likely underpowered or stalled, limiting any registrational or near-term commercial read-through.
